request.spec:
The sheet's settings assign a role to a user name: clerk (the default for any name) or steward
(ROLE_SET user=<name> role=<role>). The sheet also has a clerk limit (two decimals; blank means no
limit; SETTING_CHANGED key=clerk-limit value=<limit>). A clerk can settle a claim only when its
due is at or below the limit; above it, settling is refused with an error on the claim. A claim
whose due is n/a is within any limit. Stewards settle anything. The opener still cannot settle
their own claim.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet's settings assign a role to a user name: clerk (the default for any name) or steward
(ROLE_SET user=<name> role=<role>). The sheet also has a clerk limit (two decimals; blank means no
limit; SETTING_CHANGED key=clerk-limit value=<limit>). A clerk can settle a claim only when its
due is at or below the limit; above it, settling is refused with an error on the claim. A claim
whose due is n/a is within any limit. Stewards settle anything. The opener still cannot settle
their own claim.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Clerks can now only settle claims whose due is at or below the sheet's clerk limit, and stewards can settle anything. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**How it works**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V17__setting_role.sql`, adds a `setting` table (one value per key per sheet) and a `user_role` table. A name with no role row counts as a clerk.
- **Server:**
  - `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/settings/{key}` saves a setting. The only key is `clerk-limit`, which must be a number with up to two decimals (stored as two, so `1.5` becomes `1.50`) or blank for no limit. It writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=clerk-limit value=<limit>`.
  - `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/roles/{user}` accepts only `clerk` or `steward`. Anything else, such as `boss`, is refused, shows an error and writes nothing. A successful save writes `ROLE_SET … user=<name> role=<role>`.
  - Each has a matching `GET` that lists the sheet's settings or roles.
- **Settle rule** (in `ApplyClaimStatus`): settling works out the due as before. If the user isn't a steward, the sheet has a limit and the due is above it, the settle is refused with a 409 and nothing is saved or audited. A due of n/a is always within the limit. The rule that the opener can't settle their own claim is still checked first.
- **Screen:** two new panels on the sheet page, Settings (`features/settings/`) and Roles (`features/roles/`), using the `data-testid` names the test expects. I also extended the claim's refusal message to mention the clerk limit.

**Behaviours to know about**
- Saving the limit always writes a `SETTING_CHANGED` record, even when the value hasn't changed. One test expects this.
- Clearing the limit writes the record with an empty value (`value=`). No test covers that case.
